_comment: L1 plan Task 13 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-l1-curated-library.md): nine pieces of the 1725 Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach, a Handel Aylesford minuet, Behr's In May, a Swedish polska, an André sonatina movement and a Wanhal rondo, engraved by the Mutopia Project. Fields as documented in catalog.json's _comment. Syllabus citations: RCM Piano Syllabus 2022 Edition (https://teacherportal.rcmusic.com/getattachment/57f3734d-97e5-4777-b67e-4b1111ee31a3/piano-syllabus-2022-edition.pdf), mapped as in the plan (RCM 1-2 about our 2, 3-5 about our 3, 6-7 about our 4). Heuristic proposals and scores are from level.py.

pieces.notes: From the 1725 Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach; anonymous (Mutopia files it under J. S. Bach). Engraved from the Bach-Gesellschaft edition, vol. 43 (1894). The source has no key signature command; keyName gives the key. Two catalog patches: the source pads the half-bars 12 and 28 with an invisible spacer rest in each staff and starts the second half with \partial 4, which makes LilyPond 2.24 insert an extra beat after bar 12 and makes the converter drop the final repeat sign; the four spacers are removed, so that the upbeat completes bar 12 and the last bar complements it, as in the Bach-Gesellschaft edition, and the upbeat G gets its quarter-note duration written out (it inherited the spacer's). The LilyPond 2.24 MIDI check is exact (165/165). Accepted difference in the published-MIDI check only: the Mutopia MIDI (LilyPond 2.12) keeps the spacer beat, so every note from the second half's upbeat on sounds one quarter later; shifted by that quarter it equals the score note for note (90 notes, checked 2026-10-14).

Both hands are written in the treble clef. The source's header gives the licence in a 'mutopialicense' field; the RDF says Public Domain.

pieces.title: Polska from Norrbotten
pieces.catalogue: Traditioner af Swenska Folk-Dansar, part 1, No. 1

patches.replace: % \\unfoldRepeats removed: the MIDI check compares the notes as written

pieces.tempoSource: LilyPond \midi block of the source (quarter = 100); no printed tempo mark
pieces.levelNote: Level 3: no syllabus placement found; raised from the plan's 2 to the heuristic's proposal of 3 (8.46, above every level-2 piece of the library: two-voice right hand in thirds and sixths, dotted sixteenths, grace notes, three bars of repeated left-hand eighth-note octaves).
pieces.notes: Mutopia title 'Traditioner af Swenska Folk-Dansar, 1st part, nr 1' (a polska from Norrbotten, Sweden), engraved from the 1814 collection. The engraving is CC BY 2.5 (attribution: Erik Sjölund / Mutopia Project, piece 815); this MusicXML is shared under the same licence with the same attribution. Two catalog patches: the three bars of measured tremolo in the left hand (\repeat tremolo 6 <d d'>8) are written out as the six eighth-note octaves they abbreviate, which is what both MIDI files play; and the source's separate MIDI \score no longer unfolds the repeat, so the LilyPond 2.24 check compares the notes as written (exact, 211/211; xmlcheck counts grace notes once, so an unfolded comparison would report the second pass's grace notes). Accepted difference in the published-MIDI check only: matched 422/422 with the repeat unfolded; its two extra notes are the D5 grace notes of the second pass, for the same reason. Bar 1 shows an mf that the source hides (\once \override DynamicText #'transparent = ##t in its dynamics variable), so Mutopia's PDF prints no dynamic there; the converter does not carry the transparency over. Playback is unaffected.

pieces.title: Sonatina in C major, 1st movement
pieces.tempoSource: printed: Moderato ma con moto, no metronome mark; quarter = 104 from the LilyPond \midi block of the source, plausible for the marking
pieces.levelNote: Level 3: RCM Piano Syllabus 2022 lists the 2nd movement (Rondo) of this sonatina at Level 4 List B (about our 3); the first movement is not listed; heuristic proposes 2 (3.54).
pieces.notes: First movement only (bars 1-24): the Mutopia file also contains the Rondo, which one catalog patch removes from the three music variables before conversion, because the converter numbers the Rondo's upbeat bar '24a' and barTo alone cannot separate the movements; barTo 24 makes both MIDI checks compare the first movement (both exact, 194/194). From the 6 Sonatines progressives, Op. 34, first published by Johann André, Offenbach, 1817 or earlier (IMSLP, https://imslp.org/wiki/6_Sonatines_progressives,_Op.34_(Andr%C3%A9,_Johann_Anton)). Mutopia's header names the composer's father, Johann André (1741-1799); IMSLP and the RCM syllabus attribute Op. 34 to Johann Anton André. Engraved from an unnamed late 19th-century edition.

pieces.title: Rondo in C major
pieces.tempoSource: printed: Allegretto, no metronome mark; quarter = 108 from the LilyPond \midi block of the source, plausible for an allegretto in 2/4
pieces.levelNote: Level 3: no syllabus placement found (no Wanhal in the RCM 2022 lists), so the plan's level; heuristic proposes 3 (4.63 for the excerpt, bars 1-24; 4.34 for the whole piece).
pieces.excerpt: Bars 1-24 of 56: the C major theme up to the Fine, ending on the tonic; the F major middle section (bars 25-56) and its 'D.C. al Fine' are left out, because the score cannot play the da capo back.
pieces.notes: Johann Baptist Wanhal (Jan Křtitel Vaňhal). Engraved from an unnamed late 19th-century edition. The piece is in three parts: a C major theme (bars 1-24, marked 'Fine'), an F major middle section (bars 25-56) and 'D.C. al Fine'. The converter writes the 'D.C. al Fine' as text only (no <sound dacapo/fine>, and the app has no da capo playback), and Mutopia's own MIDI also stops at bar 56, so the whole score would play back ending in F major, with a listed duration (about 62 s) that leaves out the da capo (about 89 s with it). The excerpt keeps the theme, a musical whole of 24 bars that ends on the tonic; barTo 24 makes both MIDI checks compare bars 1-24. Writing the da capo out with a patch would diverge from the engraving.
